newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran repeats stance on Gulf islands claimed by UAE.
newsitem.headline: Iran repeats stance on Gulf islands claimed by UAE.

text.p: Iran said on Thursday three Gulf islands also claimed by the United Arab Emirates (UAE) were inseparable parts of the Islamic republic, reiterating its stance in a row straining its ties with Gulf Arab states.

But Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Mahmoud Mohammadi also said Tehran welcomed a statement by foreign ministers of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) on Wednesday hailing Iranian attempts to improve relations in the oil-producing region.

Iranian and Gulf Arab officials have made optimistic statements about improving ties since Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati visited the six GCC member states this month to invite their leaders to an Islamic summit in Tehran in December.
The GCC meeting in Riyadh welcomed what it termed "the new Iranian outlook as expressed by Dr Velayati during the tour".

Mohammadi, whose remarks were reported by Iranian state television and monitored by the British Broadcasting Corporation, said Iran believed that "cooperation among countries of the Persian Gulf region is the only way of securing stability and security in this strategic region".

But he repeated Tehran's stance that the islands of Abu Musa and the Greater and Lesser Tunb were "inseparable parts of Iran" and that it was ready for talks with the UAE to clear up any "misunderstandings".

In the Riyadh meeting the GCC -- grouping Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the UAE -- reiterated its call for an end to Iranian "occupation" of the three islands located near oil tanker routes at the entrance of the Gulf.
Earlier on Thursday, a GCC official said Gulf Arab states remained concerned about Iran's political and military policies.
"Foreign Minister Velayati was actively trying to improve relations," Abdullah al-Khulaifi, a GCC assistant secretary-general, told Reuters in Riyadh.
"But only time will tell how true his statements are... Hopefully from the Iranian side the words will match the actions. The ball is in their court."
"We have worries about Iran's militarisation, its increasing military presence on the UAE islands. We are concerned about the UAE's rights," Khulaifi said.
